Kim,

Attaching our redlines to the MSA and a draft order form. High level concerns we surfaced in legal:

- Output ownership: we can't accept a blanket assignment of downstream output — we need title to customer outputs for productization by our teams.
- Training / model use: we require an explicit opt-out for using our content to retrain vendor models; if Redwood will train on our data it must be by explicit opt-in and with a narrow scope.
- Feedback license: we proposed a limited, non-exclusive license for Redwood to use feedback for service improvement only, not for re-licensing or resale to third parties.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on those points and share suggested redline language? We are on a tight procurement window and hope to get this resolved in the next week. I'm happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through the redlines.

Thanks,

Caleb Reed
Head of Engineering, SolidBridge

Subject: Re: Redlines: MSA + Order Form (IP & training) — proposed language

Caleb / Kim — I went through SolidBridge's redlines and sketched proposed compromise language below. I attached a short text snippet with the exact redline markup (Redwood_MSARedline_Snippet.txt). High level notes and suggested language: 

1) Customer Output / Productization (proposed):
"Customer retains title to Customer Content and Customer Output. Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use aggregated, de-identified Customer Output to operate and improve the Redwood Service. Such license does not convey title and does not permit Redwood to grant Customer Output to third parties as a standalone product."

Rationale: preserves customer title for outputs they generate while allowing Redwood to use aggregated signals to improve models. This avoids an absolute assignment.

2) Model Training / Retraining (proposed):
"Redwood will not use Customer Content or Customer Output to train models that are made available to other customers or the public for production use unless Customer provides explicit, written opt-in consent for such use. Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for internal research and service quality improvements, provided such telemetry cannot be re-associated with Customer Content."

Rationale: aligns with an opt-in for production retraining while permitting telemetry for ops and diagnostics.

3) Feedback License (proposed):
"Customer grants Redwood a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use Feedback (as defined in the Agreement) to improve the Redwood Service, including internal model evaluation and tuning. Redwood will not sell or sublicense Customer Feedback as a standalone dataset to third parties. Feedback used for model improvements will be aggregated and de-identified where reasonable."

Rationale: gives Redwood operational flexibility while limiting redistribution and protecting customer IP.

Action items I recommend: 
- Laura: provide a tracked redline to the MSA + Order Form (I have a snippet attached).
- Ben: schedule a 30-min alignment call with Caleb to talk through the three clauses and confirm any carveouts for product lines.
- Kimberly: confirm timeframe for procurement and whether SolidBridge needs board/legal signoff within X days.

If any of these language points are unacceptable to SolidBridge, please call them out specifically and we can propose narrower carveouts.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
